name: Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher
administrator: HUD; run in MA by EOHLC regional agencies and local housing authorities
description: A rent subsidy for a private apartment. The program pays the landlord the part of the rent above your share.
eligibility: Low-income households, generally at or below 50% of Area Median Income (AMI). Includes adults with disabilities.
ongoing_cost: Tenant generally pays about 30% of income toward rent
how_to_apply: EOHLC list closed since Jan 13, 2025. Apply to the MassNAHRO Centralized Waiting List (affordablehousing.com/masscwl), to individual housing authorities with their own lists, or to project-based voucher properties.
notes: Lists are often closed and waits typically run 5–12 years. The Arc of Mass advises applying at 18 and joining every list. Keep contact info current or you lose your place.

name: Mainstream / Non-Elderly Disabled (NED) Vouchers
administrator: HUD; EOHLC through regional agencies; some local housing authorities
description: Section 8 vouchers set aside for adults with disabilities under 62. They work like regular vouchers.
eligibility: A household member with a disability aged 18–61; very low income; regular voucher rules apply.
ongoing_cost: About 30% of income, same as Section 8
max_benefit: Varies; EOHLC distributes up to 800 NED vouchers statewide
how_to_apply: Apply to the EOHLC Section 8 list through a regional agency; ask local housing authorities if they hold Mainstream vouchers. Bureau of Rental Assistance: 617-573-1150.
notes: Access depends on the EOHLC list, which was closed to new mobile-voucher applicants as of Jan 2025.

name: HUD Section 811 Project Rental Assistance
administrator: HUD; run in MA by EOHHS (Money Follows the Person office) with EOHLC
description: Rent help tied to specific apartments for people with disabilities who need community services.
eligibility: Extremely low income (≤30% AMI); an adult with a disability eligible for Medicaid or state community services. MA priority: MassHealth members leaving facilities.
how_to_apply: Referral only, by a case manager or provider. MFP office: 617-573-1647, MFP@mass.gov.
notes: Most autistic adults living at home are unlikely to be prioritized.

name: Federal Public Housing
administrator: HUD; run by local housing authorities
description: Apartments owned by housing authorities with rent based on income.
eligibility: Low income (HUD limits at 50% and 80% AMI); elderly, disabled and family categories.
ongoing_cost: Rent based on 30% of adjusted income
how_to_apply: Apply directly to each local housing authority. Federal public housing is not on CHAMP.
notes: Waits can be years. Boston reports 10 weeks to over 5 years depending on unit size.

name: Fair Housing Reasonable Accommodations
administrator: HUD Office of Fair Housing; MCAD in Massachusetts
description: The legal right to ask a landlord or housing authority to change a rule or the unit so a person with a disability has equal access.
eligibility: Anyone with a disability, including autism, applying for or living in covered housing.
upfront_cost: $0 to ask; can be oral or written
ongoing_cost: Subsidized housing and private buildings with 10+ units (MA law) generally pay for modifications; otherwise usually the tenant
how_to_apply: Ask the landlord or housing authority. If denied, file with HUD or MCAD.
notes: Examples: extra time to use a voucher, a home interview, an extra bedroom for equipment. MA rules: mass.gov/info-details/disability-rights-in-housing.

name: SSI living-arrangement rules
description: SSI is a monthly cash benefit often used for rent. It can be cut if someone else provides free or reduced-cost housing.
eligibility: Adults with disabilities with limited income and resources.
max_benefit: $994/month federal + $128.82 MA supplement = $1,122.82/month living independently (2026). Can be cut by up to one-third when living in another's household without paying a fair share; maximum in-kind shelter reduction $351.33 (2026).
how_to_apply: Apply at ssa.gov or a local office.
notes: Paying parents a fair share of rent can avoid the cut. Since Sept 30, 2024, food no longer counts. MA supplement source: mass.gov/doc/federal-and-state-payment-levels-for-calendar-year-cy-2026.

name: Massachusetts Rental Voucher Program (MRVP)
description: A state-funded rent voucher similar to Section 8, either mobile or tied to a unit.
eligibility: Income at or below 80% AMI; includes people with disabilities.
ongoing_cost: Tenant pays at least 30% of net monthly income
how_to_apply: Apply through CHAMP (mass.gov/champ) or on paper to local housing agencies. 617-573-1250.
notes: Very high demand and long waits.

name: Alternative Housing Voucher Program (AHVP)
description: A state rent voucher only for people with disabilities under 60. A good fit for autistic adults.
eligibility: Has a disability; under 60 when first eligible (can keep it after 60); income below about 80% AMI.
ongoing_cost: Tenant pays 25–30% of monthly income depending on utilities
how_to_apply: Apply through CHAMP or a paper application to the local housing agency. 617-573-1147.
notes: Demand is very high.

name: State Public Housing via CHAMP
description: About 41,500 state-funded public housing units, some set aside for elders and people with disabilities, all applied for through one online form.
eligibility: Income at or below 80% AMI; seniors, veterans, people with disabilities, families.
how_to_apply: Create a CHAMP account at mass.gov/champ; one application covers many waitlists.
notes: Log in at least yearly. Applications inactive for 2+ years are closed.

name: Chapter 689 Special Needs Housing
administrator: EOHLC with local housing authorities; staffed by DDS/DMH providers
description: State-owned small group homes and congregate units for adults with disabilities, staffed by DDS or DMH service providers.
eligibility: Adults who are DDS or DMH clients needing supported residential services.
how_to_apply: Through the local DDS or DMH Area Office, not the housing authority.
notes: The state's own page is out of date (still says DHCD).

name: Community Based Housing (CBH)
administrator: EOHLC with CEDAC; residents certified by MassAbility
description: State loans to developers to build integrated apartments for people with disabilities. Families rent the finished units.
eligibility: Income at or below 80% AMI, certified by MassAbility. Excludes DDS and DMH clients.
max_benefit: Developer funding up to 50% of unit cost; about $750,000 per project
how_to_apply: Ask MassAbility or an Independent Living Center about available CBH units.
notes: DDS-eligible autistic adults are generally not eligible.

name: Facilities Consolidation Fund (FCF)
description: State loans that fund community housing, often group homes, for DDS and DMH clients.
eligibility: Residents must be DDS or DMH clients.
max_benefit: Developer funding up to 50% of unit cost; 30-year 0% deferred loans
how_to_apply: Work through your regional DDS housing coordinator.
notes: Families sometimes partner with nonprofits to create FCF-funded homes.

name: Home Modification Loan Program (HMLP)
administrator: CEDAC under MassAbility, through regional agencies
description: Zero-interest loans for accessibility changes and for building an accessory apartment (ADU) for a family member with a disability.
eligibility: MA resident with a disability, or a household member with one. Gross income limit $240,000 (1 person) to $342,800 (4 people), per CEDAC 2026.
ongoing_cost: No monthly payments; repaid when the home is sold or transferred
how_to_apply: Find your regional provider and apply. CEDAC: 1-866-500-5599.
notes: ADUs under 900 sq ft are allowed by right in single-family zones since Feb 2, 2025. Loans start at $1,000.

name: RAFT Emergency Housing Assistance
description: One-time money to keep housing or move: back rent, utilities, moving costs.
eligibility: Income below 50% AMI and at risk of losing housing.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Housing Help Hub; the landlord must also submit within 21 days.
notes: Decision usually within 30 days.

name: DDS Adult Eligibility for Autism
administrator: Department of Developmental Services, Autism Division
description: The gateway to DDS services. Autistic adults without intellectual disability can qualify.
eligibility: Primary autism diagnosis, substantial limits in 3+ of 7 life areas, onset before 22. Can apply from 17.
how_to_apply: Submit the DDS Adult Eligibility Application to an Area Office. Autism Division: 617-624-7778.
notes: Autism-only services list does not include 24-hour residential.

name: DDS Residential Supports
description: Group homes with 24/7 staff, shared living with a paid caregiver, or support in the person's own apartment.
eligibility: DDS-eligible adults prioritized in their Individual Service Plan.
ongoing_cost: 24-hour residential: DDS charges 75% of SSI/SSDI and similar benefits, plus 50% of earnings above $65/month (115 CMR 3.05)
notes: Eligibility does not guarantee a placement. Residents keep at least $1,000 in liquid assets. Overview: thearcofmass.org/future/public/dds.

name: MassHealth Adult Foster Care
description: Pays a live-in caregiver, sometimes a family member, to help with daily activities at home.
eligibility: Age 16+, on MassHealth Standard or CommonHealth, needs help or supervision with at least one daily-living activity.
max_benefit: Minimum caregiver pay $25/day (Level I) or $49/day (Level II), per AFC Bulletin 32 (Apr 2024)
notes: Separate from DDS shared living.

name: MassHealth Group Adult Foster Care
description: Personal care help from agency workers for adults in qualifying housing. Covers care, not rent.
eligibility: Age 22+, MassHealth Standard or CommonHealth, needs help with at least one daily-living activity.

name: MassHousing 3% Priority Set-Aside
administrator: MassHousing with DDS, DMH, EOHLC and others
description: Sets aside units in state-financed developments for people referred by state agencies.
eligibility: People referred by DDS, DMH, EOEA or MassAbility; income up to 80% AMI.
how_to_apply: Through your DDS regional housing coordinator; MassHousing ranks by lottery.

name: Independent Living Centers
description: Free help finding and applying for accessible housing, plus peer support and advocacy.
eligibility: People with any disability.
how_to_apply: Find a center at masilc.org/findacenter or call 617-204-3600.
notes: Help with advocacy, not housing itself.

name: MCAD Housing Discrimination Complaints
description: Takes complaints about disability discrimination in housing, including refused accommodations.
eligibility: Anyone facing housing discrimination in MA.
how_to_apply: Intake in Boston, Worcester or Springfield, by mail or video. 617-994-6000.

name: Boston Housing Authority
description: Public housing, accessible units, project-based vouchers and Section 8 in Boston.
eligibility: Low income per BHA limits; background and rental-history screening.
notes: Section 8 tenant-based list closed; public housing and project-based lists open.

name: Boston Disabilities Commission: Housing
description: Points Boston residents with disabilities to housing search, home modification and legal help.
eligibility: Boston residents with disabilities.
notes: Referral only.

name: Boston Metrolist Housing Lotteries
description: Boston's search site for income-restricted rentals and homes, mostly filled by lottery.
eligibility: Income limits by unit (30%–165% AMI). Preference for accessible units.
how_to_apply: Search boston.gov/metrolist and apply to each building's lottery.
notes: Office of Housing Stability (617-635-4200) helps renters in crisis.

name: Cambridge Housing Authority
description: Family housing, senior/disabled housing, vouchers and supportive housing in Cambridge.
eligibility: ≤80% AMI for public housing; ≤50% AMI for vouchers. Senior/Disabled housing: 58+ or a qualifying disability.
ongoing_cost: Voucher holders typically pay 30% of income
notes: All four main waitlists were open when checked.

name: Worcester Housing Authority
description: Public housing, about 4,000 vouchers, accessible units and Chapter 689 group homes with DDS/DMH.
eligibility: Income-eligible households.
how_to_apply: Federal housing: worcesterha.myhousing.com. State housing: CHAMP. 508-635-3000.
notes: Also offers DMH/DDS project-based vouchers.

name: Springfield Housing Authority
description: Public housing for elderly, disabled and family households, plus MRVP and Section 8.
eligibility: Low income by family size.
how_to_apply: Paper application or CHAMP; vouchers via the Centralized Waiting List. (413) 785-4500.
notes: Closed to the public Wednesdays.

name: Autism Housing Pathways
description: Housing counseling for families of autistic adults, a 5–10 year Roadmap to Housing, and a guide to voucher lists.
eligibility: MA families of autistic and other disabled adults.
notes: Voucher guide: 18section8.org.

name: Specialized Housing, Inc.
description: Families buy a condo in one of its buildings, with support staff included in the condo fee. 12 properties in Arlington, Brookline, Cambridge and Newton.
eligibility: Adults with developmental or learning disabilities who can live semi-independently with staff checking in a few times a week.
notes: Not yet confirmed on the organization's own site, which blocks automated reading. Details from two third-party guides.

name: Adult Autism Support Centers
administrator: Northeast Arc and other DDS-funded regional centers
description: Information, referrals, workshops and support groups for autistic adults and families, including on housing.
eligibility: Adults 18+ with autism.
notes: Do not provide housing directly.

name: The Arc of Massachusetts: Housing Guidance
description: Guides on vouchers, waitlists, DDS residential options and accessory apartments.
eligibility: Open to all.
notes: Respond to housing authorities quickly; you can be dropped within 48 hours.

name: Housing Navigator Massachusetts
description: Free search engine for affordable rentals: 4,000+ properties in 260+ cities and towns.
eligibility: Open to all.
notes: Replaced the old MassAccess Housing Registry in 2022. For buying a home, see MyMassHome.

name: Lowell Housing Authority
description: Federal and state public housing, including 198 state units for families, elders, disabled and supportive housing, plus MRVP vouchers.
eligibility: Income up to 80% AMI.
ongoing_cost: Income-based rent (project-based MRVP: 40% of adjusted income)

name: Somerville Office of Housing Stability
description: Help with rent and move-in costs, housing search, and applying for affordable housing and Section 8.
eligibility: All Somerville residents; no income limit.
notes: ADA accommodations: x2059 or ADA@somervillema.gov.

name: Somerville Consolidated Rental Waitlist
description: One application covers several income-restricted rentals in Somerville.
eligibility: Income-restricted; limits vary by unit.
how_to_apply: somervillewaitlist.org during open windows (2026 window: Feb 2–Mar 2). Call 311.
notes: Only open during set windows. Watch for the next one.

name: Quincy Housing Authority
description: Elderly/disabled public housing at Crowley Court, Louis George Village, Sawyer Towers, Tobin Towers and Drohan Apartments.
eligibility: Low income; elderly or disabled.
how_to_apply: State units via CHAMP; federal units via QHA. 617-847-4350.

name: Lynn Housing Authority (LHAND)
description: Several elderly/disabled buildings plus Section 8 and tenant-based rental assistance.
eligibility: Low-income elderly or disabled adults.

name: Brockton Housing Authority
description: Public housing including elderly/disabled developments, and Section 8.
eligibility: Income up to 80% AMI; family, elderly or disabled.
ongoing_cost: Highest of 30% of adjusted income, 10% of gross income, or a $25–50 minimum
notes: Medical expenses can be deducted for elderly/disabled households.

name: Berkshire Hills Music Academy
description: Residential or day program for young adults with IDD built around music, with job and life-skills training. About 40% of students are autistic.
eligibility: Usually starts at 18–23; independent with basic self-care; no music skill needed.
ongoing_cost: 2026–27 private pay: residential $82,124 (academic year) or $104,457 (full year); day $50,177 or $74,798
notes: School districts or DDS may pay part or all.

name: Amego Adult Residential
description: Community group homes for autistic adults with programs designed by behavior analysts.
eligibility: Age 22+ with autism or a related disability.

name: Melmark New England Adult Services
description: ABA-based community residences. Building a planned community in Tewksbury: 4 homes for 20 adults, a day program and a coffee-shop business.
eligibility: Adults with autism or IDD needing moderate to significant support.
ongoing_cost: DDS, trusts or private pay; rates not published
notes: Tewksbury broke ground Feb 2025; opening date not confirmed.

name: May Institute Adult Residential
description: Community living from 24-hour supervision to drop-in support, across Cape Cod, Southeastern MA, Greater Boston and Western MA.
eligibility: Adults with autism or developmental disabilities.

name: Cardinal Cushing Centers Adult Residential
description: 24-hour residential, shared living and Adult Foster Care on the South Shore.
eligibility: Adults 22+ with disabilities.

name: Evergreen Center Adult Supports
description: Flexible residential supports for adults with autism or IDD, including those with medical or behavioral needs.
eligibility: DDS-eligible adults.

name: Riverbrook Residence
description: DDS-licensed group home with 24-hour support for women with developmental disabilities.
eligibility: Women with developmental disabilities.
how_to_apply: Call for a brochure or visit.
notes: Women only.

name: Ticket to Work
description: Free program connecting SSI or SSDI recipients with job services.
eligibility: Ages 18–64 on SSDI and/or SSI.
notes: Using the Ticket can pause medical reviews.

name: Plan to Achieve Self-Support (PASS)
description: Lets an SSI recipient set aside money for a work goal without lowering SSI.
eligibility: SSI recipients with a work goal.
max_benefit: Set-aside money is not counted toward the $2,000 SSI resource limit
how_to_apply: Form SSA-545-BK to a local office.

name: SSI / SSDI Work Incentives
description: Rules that let people keep some or all benefits while working.
eligibility: Current SSI or SSDI beneficiaries who work.
max_benefit: SSI ignores the first $65 of earnings and half the rest. Student exclusion up to $2,410/month, $9,730/year. Trial Work month $1,210; SGA $1,690/month (2026).
how_to_apply: Report earnings to SSA. Free counseling: 877-937-9675.

name: Section 1619(b) MassHealth Continuation
description: Keeps Medicaid after earnings end the SSI cash payment.
eligibility: Received SSI for at least a month, still disabled, earnings below the state threshold.

name: Work Opportunity Tax Credit
description: Federal tax credit for employers hiring VR referrals or SSI recipients.
eligibility: New hires referred by VR or Ticket to Work, or on SSI.
notes: LAPSED Dec 31, 2025. MA still accepts requests in case Congress renews it.

name: AbilityOne
description: Federal buying program from about 400 nonprofits that employ people with significant disabilities.
eligibility: People with significant disabilities hired by participating nonprofits.
how_to_apply: Find nonprofits at abilityone.gov. In MA, see WORK Inc.

name: Job Accommodation Network
administrator: U.S. DOL Office of Disability Employment Policy
description: Free, confidential advice on workplace accommodations.
eligibility: Anyone.

name: Schedule A Federal Hiring
description: Lets people with disabilities be hired into federal jobs without the usual competition.
eligibility: Intellectual, severe physical or psychiatric disability, plus job qualifications.
how_to_apply: Send resume and disability letter to an agency's Selective Placement Coordinator, or apply on USAJOBS.

name: MassHire Career Centers
description: Statewide job centers: career counseling, resumes, job search and placement, with free accommodations.
eligibility: Any job seeker.
how_to_apply: Visit your local MassHire Career Center.
notes: Funded by federal WIOA.

name: MassAbility Vocational Rehabilitation
description: The state job agency for people with disabilities: counseling, training, placement and 90 days of on-the-job support.
eligibility: MA resident with a disability that is a barrier to work.
how_to_apply: MassAbility Connect portal, local office, or 617-204-3665.
notes: Federally funded, state-run.

name: Pre-Employment Transition Services
description: Job exploration, work-readiness training and work-based learning for students.
eligibility: Students with disabilities ages 14–21.
how_to_apply: Local MassAbility office or school Pre-ETS provider. 617-204-3600.

name: NextGen Careers
description: Mentoring, benefits advice, apprenticeships and internships for young adults.
eligibility: Ages 18–30 with disabilities.
how_to_apply: Contact MassAbility (Boston, Braintree, Lawrence, Lowell, Springfield, Worcester).
notes: Reported at capacity as of May 2025.

name: DDS Employment & Day Supports
description: Funds individual and group supported employment plus community day programs.
eligibility: DDS-eligible adults, including autism-only. Usually starts at 22.
how_to_apply: DDS Adult Eligibility Application at 17–18. Autism Division: 617-624-7778.

name: MassHealth CommonHealth
description: Full MassHealth coverage for adults with disabilities with no income limit.
eligibility: Disability determined by SSA or MassHealth; no work requirement under 65.

name: Work Without Limits
description: Free benefits counseling, Ticket to Work services and a job board.
eligibility: SSI/SSDI beneficiaries 14+ in its service area.
notes: Funded by SSA.

name: MA Disability Employment Tax Credit
description: State tax credit for employers who hire people with disabilities.
eligibility: Worker holds a MassAbility certificate and has worked 12 consecutive months.
max_benefit: Up to $5,000 first year; $2,000 later years
notes: Still active while federal WOTC is lapsed.

name: Young Adults with Disabilities Grant
description: State grants for job training, placement and coaching through local partners.
eligibility: Ages 18–35 with disabilities.
how_to_apply: Contact a grantee: Berkshire County Arc, Blackstone Valley Hub, Curry College, JVS, Northeast Arc, Polus Center.

name: Massachusetts Autism Commission
description: Advisory body that publishes a transition guide for ages 14–22.
eligibility: Information only.

name: Boston Disabilities Commission: Employment
description: Referrals to employment programs and a disability employment webinar series.
eligibility: Boston residents with disabilities.

name: Cambridge Commission for Persons with Disabilities
description: Free disability information and advocacy, including on employment.
eligibility: Cambridge residents.
notes: Referral only.

name: WORK Inc.
description: New England's largest AbilityOne contractor. Employs about 120 people with disabilities at federal buildings.
eligibility: People with disabilities, often referred by DDS or MassAbility.

name: The Caning Company
description: Chair-caning business offering paid training to people with disabilities.
eligibility: People served by Northeast Arc.

name: Heritage Shredding
description: Secure document shredding done by trained workers with disabilities.
eligibility: People served by Northeast Arc.

name: Northeast Arc Employment Services
description: Career planning, job development and coaching on the North Shore, including a pizza-shop training program.
eligibility: Typically DDS/MassAbility-funded.

name: Prospect Meadow Farm
description: Working farm giving paid jobs to adults with IDD, including autism.
eligibility: DDS-eligible; referral by DDS or school.
notes: Also sites in Pittsfield.

name: Gateway Arts
description: Professional art studio for nearly 100 artists with disabilities.
eligibility: Adults with disabilities.

name: The Price Center & Kindness Café
description: Job training and coaching; Kindness Café trains baristas with IDD.
eligibility: Adults with IDD.
notes: 95% still employed after a year (program's own figure).

name: Post-22 & Ben's Beans
description: Training and jobs for adults with IDD, including a coffee shop staffed by participants.
eligibility: Adults 22+ with IDD.

name: Aspire Works Internships
description: 10–12 week internships with 60+ Boston-area employers, plus career coaching.
eligibility: Adults 18+ on the autism spectrum.
upfront_cost: Scholarships for students of certain MA colleges; other fees not published
notes: Partners include Fidelity and Liberty Mutual.

name: Triangle, Inc. & Prism
description: Group supported employment at competitive wages; Prism serves autistic adults 22+.
eligibility: Adults with disabilities.
notes: Sites in Malden, Salem, Randolph.

name: Easterseals MA Job Placement
description: Job search and retention support via MassAbility referrals.
eligibility: MassAbility consumers in its regions.

name: JVS Transitions to Work
description: Free job training and internships at employers like CVS and Boston Children's.
eligibility: Ages 17–35 with a disability or IEP.

name: Best Buddies Jobs
description: Helps people with IDD find and keep paid jobs.
eligibility: People with IDD in MA/RI.

name: Charles River Center
description: Job placement and one-on-one job coaching for adults with IDD and autism in MetroWest.
eligibility: Adults with IDD and/or autism.

name: AANE WorkMAP / LifeMAP Coaching
description: One-to-one job coaching for autistic adults: job search, interviewing and keeping a job. Free grant slots for some young adults.
eligibility: Autistic adults and older teens. Free WorkMAP slots: ages 18–35, low-to-moderate income, living in Boston, Cambridge, Chelsea, Quincy, Randolph or Somerville.
upfront_cost: Free for grant slots; otherwise a $325–$375 intake meeting
how_to_apply: Book a free call at aane.org.
notes: AANE pages list two different fees. Confirm the current rate.

name: Minute Man Arc Employment Services
description: Individual job placement with coaching, group work crews and customized jobs with 40+ local employers.
eligibility: Referral from DDS, MassAbility, DMH or schools; private pay accepted.
upfront_cost: Usually paid by the referring agency

name: Seven Hills ASPiRE!
description: Job assessment, coaching and placement, plus group supported employment.
eligibility: Adults with IDD, autism or brain injury; referral through DDS or MassAbility.
max_benefit: Up to 15 hours/week of vocational training (day supports)

name: South Shore Industries
description: DDS-supported day program building toward paid jobs with partners like Trader Joe's and Market Basket.
eligibility: Adults 22+ with disabilities.

name: Open Sky I/DD Employment Services
description: Career planning, coaching and long-term job support for adults with IDD and autism.
eligibility: Adults in Worcester, Blackstone Valley and Norfolk County.

name: Riverside Industries
description: Job placement plus an on-site packaging and production department serving clients like Yankee Candle.
eligibility: People with IDD; partners with DDS and MassAbility.

name: Berkshire County Arc Employment
description: Job placement and support with 50+ regional businesses in Berkshire County and the Pioneer Valley.
eligibility: People with developmental disabilities, brain injury or autism.
notes: Figures date from 2019.

name: Cooperative Production (CO-OP)
description: Job exploration, coaching and help starting a small business in southeastern MA.
eligibility: Adults and transition students with IDD or brain injury; funded by DDS, MassAbility and schools.

name: Project SEARCH (neba)
description: School-to-work internships at a host business for young adults with disabilities.
eligibility: Young adults with disabilities.
notes: Call to confirm the current host sites.

name: futureBOS Youth Jobs (formerly SuccessLink)
administrator: City of Boston Youth Employment and Opportunity
description: Boston's summer and year-round youth jobs program.
eligibility: Boston residents ages 14–24.
notes: No disability-specific track listed. Ask for accommodations.

name: Worcester Accessibility Division
description: Free help on disability rights, including workplace accommodations.
eligibility: Worcester residents and employers.
notes: Referral and rights help only.

name: Springfield Office for Citizens with Disabilities
description: City referral office for residents with disabilities.
eligibility: Springfield residents.
notes: Referral only.

name: Somerville Commission for Persons with Disabilities
description: Handles ADA complaints and reasonable accommodation requests.
eligibility: Somerville residents.

name: Newton YouthWorks Internships
description: Paid summer internships for Newton teens who face barriers to work.
eligibility: Ages 16–18 who can apply and interview on their own.
notes: Not a fit for people who need high support.

name: Venture Autism Employment Services
description: Job training and placement for young adults with autism.
eligibility: Young adults 18+ with autism.
